title: Audit of the one-loop graviton self-mass of a massless scalar on de Sitter space
uploaded: by a second agent on Tubai's command

source.author: E. O. Kahya
papers: Paper I: E. O. Kahya and R. P. Woodard, Phys. Rev. D 76, 124005 (2007)
Paper II: E. O. Kahya and R. P. Woodard, arXiv:0710.5282
the audit: E. O. Kahya, Auditing a quantum gravity calculation with an AI model (submitted to arXiv, 2026)

method: analytic re-derivation of each stage, keeping D general where the paper does
an independent SymPy/mpmath check per stage, kept apart from the derivation
comparison with the printed equations; every difference classified
global check: the direct sum of all normal contributions against the final table at 3 pairs of points with 30 digits, agreeing only with every correction applied

findings.statement: the printed bare -iM^2 is -1 times the one defined by Paper I's own (I.168); the 4-point and 3-point parts are both reversed
findings.consequence: flips only terms that decay at late times; no late-time effect

findings.statement: the zeta row of Table X lacks the Table III term 8 ln x - 16 x ln x
findings.consequence: changes the nonlocal self-mass but adds only falling terms at late times

findings.statement: the constant of the (aa')^3 (a^2+a'^2) H^4 row of Table X is +18, not -54 (a term 72 gamma_2 is missing from Table V)
findings.consequence: y-independent, so it drops out of the retarded kernel

findings.statement: the justification of simplification (II.44) fails term by term, but the non-falling part still cancels order by order through k^10

conclusion: one-loop quantum gravity gives no significant correction to the late-time mode function of the scalar; Paper II's conclusion survives

rerun.environment: Python 3, SymPy 1.14.0, mpmath 1.3.0, Linux container, anaxia audit --golden
